text:
Context: Advanced Probability Theory Seminar, Zhejiang University
Date: Fall 2025

Topics covered:

Tail \(\sigma\)-fields, Kolmogorov’s 0–1 Law, and the Hewitt–Savage 0–1 Law.
Kolmogorov’s maximal inequality and the three-series theorem.
Strong laws of large numbers under different moment assumptions.
Cramér’s theorem, including moment generating functions, Legendre transforms, exponential tilting, and change-of-measure arguments.






Context: Weekly Statistics Seminar, Prof. Lijun Wang’s Group
Date: Fall 2025

Topics covered:

Model-X knockoffs and finite-sample false discovery rate control.
Multiple-run aggregation methods, including e-value-based derandomization and selection-frequency approaches.
Empirical power collapse under extreme heavy-tailed designs.
The zero-dilution mechanism, in which unstable single-run selections are diluted across repeated knockoff runs.
The role of internal threshold calibration in restoring power while maintaining FDR control.

title: Jiahao Tian
text:
Hi! My name is Jiahao Tian. I am an undergraduate student majoring in Statistics at the School of Mathematical Sciences, Zhejiang University.
My research interests lie at the intersection of high-dimensional inference, uncertainty quantification, and theoretical statistics. I am particularly interested in developing statistically principled methods that remain reliable under distribution shift, heavy-tailed distributions, and other forms of model misspecification.

Research Interests

High-dimensional statistical inference
Conformal prediction and uncertainty quantification
Multiple testing and false discovery rate control
Distribution shift and robust statistics

title: Research & Projects
text:
Advisor: Prof. Lijun Wang, School of Mathematical Sciences, Zhejiang University
Period: Sep. 2025 – Present
Status: First-author manuscript in preparation
Keywords: Model-X Knockoffs · False Discovery Rate · Multiple-Run Aggregation · Heavy-Tailed Distributions · Extreme Value Theory

Overview
This project studies the robustness of multiple-knockoff aggregation procedures under extreme heavy-tailed distributions. While aggregation is designed to improve reproducibility across randomized knockoff runs, our results show that it can amplify instability when individual runs become overly sparse or highly variable.
Main Contributions

Conducted a systematic comparison of e-value-, voting-, p-value-, and data-splitting-based knockoff aggregation methods under Gaussian, moderately heavy-tailed, and Cauchy regimes.
Identified a zero-dilution mechanism in which unstable and severely truncated single-run selections cause occasional signal discoveries to be diluted below the final aggregation threshold.
Developed an asymptotic explanation using regular variation, exact null sign symmetry, concentration inequalities, and Extreme Value Theory.
Linked the numerical dominance of null features in sparse high-dimensional settings to threshold inflation and vanishing signal-selection probabilities.
Investigated robust feature-importance statistics and the role of internal threshold calibration in recovering statistical power.






Advisor: Prof. Guanhua Chen, University of Wisconsin–Madison
Period: Mar. 2026 – Present
Status: First-author manuscript in preparation
Keywords: Conformal Prediction · Covariate Shift · Distributional Balancing · Characteristic Function Distance · Fourier Analysis · UACQR

Overview
This project develops response-free distributional balancing methods for conformal calibration under covariate shift. The main idea is to reweight labeled source calibration covariates toward an unlabeled target population and use the resulting weighted score distribution to approximate target-domain calibration without requiring accurate pointwise density-ratio estimation.
Main Contributions

Developed a distributionally balanced conformal calibration framework that aligns source calibration covariates with an unlabeled target sample.
Specialized the framework to Characteristic Function Distance (CFD) balancing and studied how spectral decay affects the representation of covariate-dependent conformity-score distributions.
Used Fourier analysis to compare Gaussian, product-Laplace, Matérn, and energy-type balancing geometries through their induced smoothness and frequency-domain behavior.
Implemented the weighting and calibration pipeline for Split Conformal Prediction, Conformalized Quantile Regression, UACQR-S, and UACQR-P.
Contributed to the technical verification and revision of a general score-distribution and approximate coverage-error bound involving residual imbalance, function-class approximation, finite target-sample uncertainty, and effective sample size.
Designed theory-aligned simulations evaluating coverage, interval efficiency, score-distribution error, imbalance, and weight concentration under varying overlap and score smoothness.

title: Research & Projects
text:
💻 Selected Computational Projects

CNN Forward Inference Engine in C

Period: Spring 2025
Tech Stack: C · CNN Inference · Channel Pruning · Binary I/O

Project Summary

Implemented a convolutional neural network forward-inference engine from scratch in C.
Built binary input and parameter-loading routines and implemented the forward computation without relying on high-level deep-learning frameworks.
Reduced inference latency by approximately 75% through channel pruning while maintaining approximately 99% classification accuracy.




Uncertainty Quantification for PDEs on Random Domains

Period: Fall 2025
Tech Stack: Python · Stochastic Galerkin Methods · Karhunen–Loève Expansions · Polynomial Chaos

Project Summary

Reproduced numerical methods for elliptic stochastic partial differential equations defined on random domains.
Used stochastic mappings to transform random-domain problems into equivalent formulations on a fixed reference domain.
Applied Karhunen–Loève expansions and Legendre polynomial chaos to represent geometric uncertainty and propagate it through the PDE solver.
